faqs.question: What is MOFA Attestation?
faqs.answer: MOFA attestation (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) is a core step before many embassy legalizations. SK Immigration explains order of operations so you do not pay twice for out-of-sequence stamps.

faqs.question: How long does attestation take?
faqs.answer: Simple chains may finish in several working days; embassy queues and incomplete prior stamps take longer. We give a realistic range after seeing your document list.

faqs.question: Do you handle HEC / MOFA / embassy sequencing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Wrong order is the most expensive mistake — we map the chain for your destination before you pay for stamps.

faqs.question: Can attestation be done for Saudi employment?
faqs.answer: Yes — educational and personal documents for Saudi often need MOFA and Saudi Embassy steps, sometimes with Musadaqa/QVP depending on the paper type.

faqs.question: Where can I see the full attestation hub?
faqs.answer: Visit our attestation overview page for Musadaqa, QVP, Apostille, MOFA and embassy options in one place.

body:
Overview

MOFA attestation (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) is a core step before many embassy legalizations. SK Immigration explains order of operations so you do not pay twice for out-of-sequence stamps.

Requirements

  • Original documents or certified copies as required
  • Clear scans and consistent name spellings vs passport
  • Prior stamps (notary/HEC/IBCC/MOFA) in the correct order
  • Destination country rules (Apostille vs embassy legalization)

Process

  1. Document audit and destination check
  2. Local verification steps (as applicable)
  3. MOFA / Apostille pathway
  4. Embassy attestation if required
  5. Delivery checklist for visa or employer use

Documents we commonly handle

  • Degrees and transcripts
  • Marriage and birth certificates
  • Police character certificates
  • Commercial papers (case by case)

Fees & timeline

Government and embassy fees vary by document type. SK Immigration quotes service support separately after reviewing your list. Timelines depend on authority queues.

Common mistakes

  • Paying for embassy stamps before MOFA/Apostille is done
  • Name mismatches across documents
  • Using photocopies when originals are required
  • Assuming every country accepts Apostille
